result.state_0: R(X,Z) with protected witness side Z and live semantic interface X
result.forward_reencoding: Y=B(X), with B(x1,x2)=(x1 XOR x2,x2); introduce Y definitionally and eliminate X by the exact inverse
result.theorem: Any progress potential invariant under definitional/bijective re-encoding must have Phi(state_0)=Phi(state_1). Therefore it cannot strictly decrease on every allowed macro-step when reversible re-encodings are allowed. Any potential that does strictly decrease on this step is representation-sensitive and fails the anti-alias requirement.

semantic_interface_gold_standard.definition: For a relation R(B,W), let N_R(B|W) be the number of distinct residual continuation relations R_b(W) obtained by fixing b on B; define mu=ceil(log2 N_R).
semantic_interface_gold_standard.property: mu is invariant under bijective reparameterization of B.
semantic_interface_gold_standard.equality_zipper_control: For R(X,Z)=[Z=X], N=2^n and mu=n. After any invertible re-encoding Y=B(X), N and mu remain unchanged.

finite_killer.conclusion: zero semantic progress despite variable-name replacement
